newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong Democrats raise funds in North America.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong Democrats raise funds in North America.

text.p: Hong Kong's Democratic Party, often seen as an arch-foe of China, has raised nearly HK$750,000 (US$97,000) in donations in North America, a party member said on Monday.
Lee Wing-tat said the money had come from Chinese communities during a 15-stop fund-raising tour of the United States and Canada by party leaders earlier this month.
"Yes, we have raised close to the equivalent of HK$750,000," Lee told Reuters.
The fund-raisers included party leader Martin Lee and his deputy Szeto Wah, who have been branded as subversives by Beijing.

Britain hands Hong Kong back to China at midnight on June 30 and the Democratic Party has been in the forefront of political clashes with China over its plans to curb democracy and civil rights laws in the territory.
The Democratic Party was the most popular political group during elections for the territory's Legislative Council in 1995.
Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp has assailed a 60-member provisional chamber chosen by a Beijing-anointed caucus to replace the Legislative Council after the colony reverts to Chinese rule.
The Democrats have re-applied for permission to hold a rally in Hong Kong's main business district on June 30 after an earlier application was rejected by authorities, Lee Wing-tat said.
"We are applying again to hold a rally...we were rejected two weeks ago. But it was just a political decision," Lee said.
"We want to celebrate the handover, and on the other hand, we want to use it to state our position on democracy, human rights and the rule of law," he said.
China has provoked jitters in the territory of 6.4 million people over plans to have the interim chamber roll back laws protecting civil liberties and democracy.
